subject: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / SLA & deployment follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finova.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finova.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / SLA & deployment follow-up

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a concise proposal and pricing for your evaluation committee.

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary use case: real-time customer conversational flows (single-turn + short multi-turn support dialogs).
- Performance ask: production pilot target p95 inference latency in the 100–200 ms range for ~512-token contexts.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement expects a clear unit-cost target for comparison (pilot budget constraints).
- Deployment preference: security indicated a preference for Private (VPC) or Redwood Dedicated with strict network isolation; this is still to be confirmed by your security/procurement teams.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + audit logs + KMS integration required; data residency TBD.

Clarifying questions / action items for you:
1) Can you confirm the hard p95 latency target for the pilot? Is 200 ms p95 acceptable as a max for the initial pilot, with a target of <=150 ms for steady-state?
2) Do you have an explicit cost target (e.g., $/1k tokens or $/session) that procurement will use to compare vendors? If not, we can provide a few scenarios (pilot vs production) for your rubric.
3) Which deployment mode is preferred after pilot: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) or Redwood Private (VPC / customer-controlled infra)? Security has referenced Private, but we know that Dedicated can often meet isolation needs with faster time-to-value.
4) Economic buyer / procurement contacts: can you confirm who needs to sign off on the commercial terms?

Attachments: I've attached a short rubric template (Finova-Decision-Rubric.xlsx) if you want to drop in numbers; I'll also attach a short pricing note comparing Dedicated vs Private.

Next steps: if you can answer items 1–4 above, I'll produce a one-page proposal (performance targets, estimated unit costs for pilot and annual commit options, and a recommended rollout plan) by EOD Thursday.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finova.com>, procurement@finova.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / SLA & deployment follow-up

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Latency: for the pilot, 200 ms p95 is acceptable. Our long-term bar is ~150 ms p95, but we don't expect that on day one. We care most about consistent tail latency rather than average.

2) Cost: procurement prefers a per-1k-token comparable metric; as a rough starting point they expect something in the $0.01–$0.05 per 1k-token equivalent range for pilot tooling (we know this is approximate). Please present a few scenarios (low/med/high throughput) in your proposal.

3) Deployment: Security is leaning Private (VPC) because some customer data will be scoped as sensitive. If Dedicated can provide the same network isolation and KMS integration, we're open to that path if it shortens time-to-production.

4) Decision / procurement: Tom (cc'd) is the technical economic buyer. Procurement is procurement@finova.com and will own contract review. Security will loop in separately (I'll forward them your SOC 2 docs).

5) Throughput: pilot target is 50–100 queries per second with bursts up to ~200 rps for short windows (promotions). That will affect batching and cost recommendations.

I've uploaded a filled version of the decision rubric — see attached. Let us know if you want to walk through it on Thursday.

—Sara
Sara Patel
Sr. Product Manager, AI | Finova

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / SLA & deployment follow-up

Thanks Sara — super helpful. A few concrete notes based on your answers:

- Latency: we'll size the pilot config to target <=200 ms p95 out of the gate and provide a remediation plan (kernel selection / quantization profile / KV caching) to move toward ~150 ms p95 for steady-state.
- Cost: we'll include per-1k-token and per-100k-requests scenarios. Preliminary ballpark (pilot-sized Dedicated): ~$0.02–$0.04 per 1k tokens depending on batching, cache hit rate, and model choice. Private (VPC) + higher isolation will add an uplift — we'll show the delta in the proposal.
- Throughput: we'll size for sustained 50–100 qps and provide burst capacity to ~200 rps; we'll note autoscaling and warm pools to preserve latency SLOs.
- Compliance: standard SOC 2 + KMS + audit logs supported. If you need EU data residency, that adds constraints — please confirm region per-account.

I've attached a short one-pager that compares Dedicated vs Private pricing and timelines. Next step: we'll produce a one-page proposal + cost scenarios and suggest a follow-up call on Thursday 8/20 10:00–10:30 PT to review with Tom and procurement. Does that time work?

If Thursday works, I'll include David (solutions lead) to walk throughput sizing and Neha (security lead) to answer the SOC 2 / KMS questions live.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
